sections.h2: Your choices for selling a Cottage Grove house
sections.html:
Owners here can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a direct cash offer. Each suits a different set of circumstances.

If the house is in good repair and you are in no hurry, a listing goes after the top price. Cash fits a seller who needs to close quickly, whose house has open permits or postponed work, or who has a private well and wants fewer hurdles. Collect the permit history, well results, the utility estimate and the tax balance before you talk to any buyer, and compare written offers against what an agent expects your house to bring.

sections.h2: Cottage Grove housing at a glance
sections.html:
Cottage Grove, in Washington County, lies roughly 10 miles south of Saint Paul beside the Mississippi. U.S. Highways 10 and 61 and Interstate 494 serve it, and the Minneapolis-Saint Paul airport is about half an hour away. The 2025 population estimate is 43,604, up 12.3 percent from the 2020 base of 38,839. Most of the city was built in the last half century, so your house competes with many similar listings.

Households average 2.84 people and a quarter of residents are under 18, so buyers lean toward families who care about school boundaries and yard space.

The South Washington County School District runs the public schools. Park High School and East Ridge High School serve most high school students, and Cottage Grove Middle School and Oltman Middle School serve most middle school students. Six elementary schools sit in the city: Armstrong, Cottage Grove, Crestview, Grey Cloud, Hillside and Pine Hill.

Ravine Regional Park, River Oaks golf course and the city's ice arena add to demand. 3M has run a production facility in town since 1947, which gives many residents a workable commute to both downtowns and the Interstate 494 strip in Bloomington.

sections.h2: Does PFAS contamination affect a home sale?
sections.html:
It can, mainly if the house runs on a private well. The Minnesota Pollution Control Agency says 3M chemicals containing PFOS, PFOA and other PFAS were made at the Chemolite plant in Cottage Grove, and that 3M waste disposal at four east metro sites contaminated groundwater across a large part of the region.

Cottage Grove is on the agency's list of communities where private wells are sampled. Sampling of eligible private wells is free to homeowners under the state's settlement with 3M, and eligible wells can receive point-of-entry treatment systems that the agency installs and maintains. If you own a well, request testing through the agency's online form and keep the results with your sale paperwork. A buyer with a well will ask for them.

Cottage Grove takes permit applications online, and the Building Division at 651-458-2804 handles inspections and permits. The residential permit list covers accessory structures over 200 square feet, additions, remodels, decks, demolition, pools, solar, roofing, siding, window replacement and door replacement, plus mechanical, plumbing and electrical work.

  • Contractors may work Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. and on Saturday from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m.
  • Electrical inspections are handled by a contracted outside inspector, so schedule them separately.
  • The Code Enforcement Officer handles property maintenance concerns and runs the city's rental licensing program, so an owner with tenants should call the Building Division before a sale.

Close out any open permits before listing so a buyer's lender or inspector has nothing to question late in the deal.

Title and closing companies request a utility estimate from the city, and the final amount is collected at the closing table. The city runs an online form for this, the Utility Billing Request for Real Estate Closing, and it covers both current and outstanding city utility bills.

Tell your closing agent early so the request goes in before the closing date.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Washington County
sections.html:
Your buyer's deed is filed with the Washington County Recorder, whose office is in the Government Center in Stillwater. Expect a $46 recording charge and state deed tax of $3.30 for each thousand dollars of the price. A $5 conservation fee is added, and a $54 well certificate is needed when the deed does not carry a well statement. When the price is under $3,000 the tax is a flat $1.65. Certain deeds also require an electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value.

The county reminds parties that most parcels here are abstract property, which makes a careful title search worth doing before closing. Research staff in the Government Center keep weekday hours from 8 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Separately, Minnesota Statutes 103I.235 requires you to give the buyer a written note about any wells you know of before you sign.

Tax on most real property comes due in two equal halves, May 15 and October 15. Values are set as of January 2. By March 31 the county mails statements along with a valuation notice for the following year, and a Proposed Property Tax Notice goes out in mid-November.

A homestead that misses the first-half date is charged a 2 percent penalty starting May 16. Anything still unpaid on January 2 turns delinquent and accrues 8 percent annual interest. Payment options are eCheck at $0.75, card at 2.35 percent, mail, bank bill pay or the Government Center drop box. To discuss your value, call an assessor at 651-430-6175.

When taxes are owed at the sale, the title company can pay them from your proceeds at closing, so ask for the balance early.

faqs.q: Can I get my private well tested for PFAS in Cottage Grove?
faqs.a: Yes. Cottage Grove is among the east metro communities where the state samples private wells, and sampling of eligible wells is free to homeowners. Use the online request form on the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency's well sampling page.

faqs.q: Who pays the city utility bill at a Cottage Grove closing?
faqs.a: You do, from your proceeds. The closing company asks the city for an estimate on its Utility Billing Request for Real Estate Closing form and settles current and outstanding amounts at the table.

faqs.q: What are the deed recording costs in Washington County?
faqs.a: A $46 recording charge, deed tax of $3.30 per thousand dollars of price, and a $5 conservation fee. Add $54 for a well certificate if the deed has no well statement.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In two halves, May 15 and October 15. A homestead that pays the first half late is charged 2 percent starting May 16.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace the roof or windows before selling in Cottage Grove?
faqs.a: Yes. Roofing, siding, window replacement and door replacement are all on the city's residential permit list, and applications go through the online permitting site. Call 651-458-2800 or email building@cottagegrovemn.gov for help with an account.
